questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
- Academics, especially wanting to improve my "legal english" and the specific courses offered
- The national language is English
- Wanting to experience an Asian country and a culture very different from my own

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All information was provided really.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a webinar before arrival, there were multiple e-mails and fliers about course registration, studentpass (visa) and housing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Some of the information was a little unclear, but overall it worked out well.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I stayed at Sheares Hall, but there are multiple halls and houses on Kent Ridge Campus.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: My hall had an mandatory meal plan, but it was very cheap. There was also a tea kitchen on my floor and each "block" had a larger shared kitchen. Although, not a lot of students cooked because it is very cheap to buy food (but not groceries).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
I would say that if you get to stay at uTown or PGPR student housing seems fine - if not, you should be prepared for the worst.
If there is no airconditioner your clothes, shoes and so on will grow mold due to the humidity. I got most out by washing, but it gets everywhere - even my headphones got infested. I heard from other exchange students that they had black mold in their ceilings, which just got painted over. It is not allowed to install your own airconditioner, but most local students do so.

Specifically, in Sheares Hall there was an issue with rain coming through the window. At my hall there was also found a worm in the food in the dinning hall.

I think with student housing at NUS you can either be very lucky or very unlucky. Some struggled more with insects and mold than others. The upside is that the rent is pretty cheap.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You start by requesting courses when you are registering at the university. At this time you usually get three courses, and if you need a fourth course, you will request this at the start of the semester. Then there is an appeals round if you for example didn't get enough courses or your exams overlap.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't really remember, but I'm sure there was an e-mail adresse you could contact.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Pretty satisfied

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It takes a long time and you are responsible for making sure that your schedule works. However, NUSmods is helpful for this, as it has a "timetable" feature where you can add and remove courses. Also keep in mind that there are different examinations types - some a research papers, some are written sit in and some a written take home exams.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The teachers were amazing and all very accomplished in their fields.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I think that the level of the classes varied a lot since they are elective courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching style was quite similar to UCPH, as NUS also uses seminar classes. The professor would talk and ask questions and some times there would be student presentations.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Energy arbitration
Singapore Legal History
Public International Law
Regulation of Digital Platforms (intensive course)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Energy arbitration was an amazing course. The teachers are very competent and the topics were very interesting (at least to me).

For an understanding of Singapore, I would really recommend Singapore Legal History. It was really nice to learn about Singapore's history. It was also nice to write a research paper as the final exam.

questions.answer: Dehumidifier

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Eating out at hawker centers or the canteens on campus is cheap, but buying groceries or going to a restaurant or for drinks is expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There were a lot of events for exchange students arranged by NUS and also the NUS law Student's International Relations Committee (LSIRC).

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: There is always a lot going on at NUS and with the other exchange students. Join whatever whatsapp groups suits your interest and then you can go the different events with other exchange students - ie. hiking group, sky diving group, travel group, off campus partying groups.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
You should definitely take a trip to Kuala Lumpur. If you are up for it a lot of students take an overnight bus (5 ish hours). Malaysia in general is very cheap. Going to Johor Bahru just on the other side of the border is also very popular. Singapore is generally ideal for traveling East Asia!

Also most museums in Singapore are free for students, so you should take advantage of that!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was not really an issue.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would say befriending the locals in your classes is the best way to go.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Singaporeans are generally reserved, so you have to make an effort to get to know them.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The many diverse cultures that make up Singapore. It was very interesting to experience how many different cultures lived harmoniously in Singapore.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Singapore is place with a lot of rules and laws, so make sure to be respectful of them.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Downloade the apps: uNivUS, NUS NextBus, Telegram and Grab (basically Uber).

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I think the best part of exchange has been meeting other exchange students and Singaporean students! Getting to experience the unique culture in Singapore was also really great. Lastly, NUS has some truly amazing and accomplished teachers that are very passionate about their fields.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I think the biggest challenge for me was that the assessment was ongoing. This means that you are constantly evaluated for class participation and midterms. This was a big change from what I am used to back home.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer:
There were som challenges housing wise, but apart form that my stay in Singapore was amazing. I'm sure that anyone going will have an incredible experience!

Going on exchange is a lot of work but so worth it:)

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
